course_goals.text: Analyze the foundational concepts, historical evolution, and inherent challenges of Extended Reality (XR) systems, including psychological dimensions and cultural applications.
Design and analyze the complete architecture of immersive XR systems, integrating hardware components, tracking mechanisms, and user-centric software development principles.
Evaluate the influence of human sensory perception and physiological processes on XR design, focusing on visual, auditory, and non-visual factors to enhance immersion.
Apply optimization techniques and rigorous empirical methods to enhance XR performance, mitigate physiological discomfort, and implement complex systems using industry tools.

L01.lecture_goal: Explain the foundational concepts, applications, and scope of XR technologies while outlining the course structure.

objectives.text: You'll be able to explain the core concepts, applications, and differences between Augmented Reality, Augmented Virtuality, and Mixed Reality.
You'll be able to justify the growing commercial and technological importance of XR.
You'll be able to outline the course objectives, focus areas, and learning methodology for XR systems.

L02.lecture_goal: Analyze the application domains and system categories of extended reality.

objectives.text: You'll be able to identify and describe the major application domains and assess the market potential of extended reality and immersive technologies.
You'll be able to compare and contrast non-immersive, semi-immersive, and fully immersive VR systems.

L03.lecture_goal: Analyze the fundamental concepts, classifications, and comparative uses of Augmented and Virtual Reality systems.

objectives.text: You'll be able to identify and describe the diverse application domains of Augmented Reality and differentiate between marker-based and markerless AR applications.
You'll be able to compare and contrast the system categories and application focuses of Virtual Reality (VR) and Augmented Reality (AR).

L04.lecture_goal: Distinguish between Virtual Reality and non-VR systems by applying its core characteristics.

objectives.text: You'll be able to define virtual reality and identify its three defining characteristics.
You'll be able to apply the three defining characteristics to classify systems as Virtual Reality or not.

L05.lecture_goal: Differentiate between the various types of immersive reality systems (AR, VR, and MR).

objectives.text: You'll be able to identify and explain the defining characteristics of Augmented Reality and compare the fundamental differences between AR and VR systems.
You'll be able to analyze the conflicting definitions of Mixed Reality and recap the key differences among VR, AR, and MR systems.

L06.lecture_goal: Analyze the historical evolution of virtual and augmented reality technologies.

objectives.text: You'll be able to identify the four historical phases of VR/AR and the foundational inventions that laid the groundwork for virtual reality.
You'll be able to trace the key historical milestones of VR development, including hardware and software advancements from the 1990s to 2015.
You'll be able to identify the recent growth phases and key industry milestones in the modern VR landscape.

L07.lecture_goal: Analyze the historical evolution of Augmented Reality and Virtual Reality systems.

objectives.text: You'll be able to describe the foundational phases and trace the early evolution of AR and VR systems, identifying key research milestones.
You'll be able to trace the evolution of AR tools during the mid-1990s and identify key milestones in the historical development of AR and VR.

L08.lecture_goal: Analyze the foundational concepts, challenges, and psychological dimensions of virtual and augmented reality systems.

objectives.text: You'll be able to summarize the foundational concepts, definitions, and applications of VR and AR systems, and distinguish between the technological and psychological challenges of VR systems.
You'll be able to explain the definition and components of immersion, and compare and distinguish between immersion and presence in virtual reality systems.

L09.lecture_goal: Understand the key technological and psychological challenges facing the development and adoption of VR and AR systems.

objectives.text: You'll be able to analyze the challenges of achieving presence in VR and explain the technical requirements and phases necessary for successful AR implementation.
You'll be able to summarize the major technological and psychological challenges in VR and AR systems.

L10.lecture_goal: Analyze the definition, symptoms, and contributing factors of cybersickness.

objectives.text: You'll be able to define cybersickness, identify its symptoms, and outline the three areas of study.
You'll be able to identify and describe the internal factors contributing to cybersickness.
You'll be able to identify and describe the external hardware factors contributing to cybersickness.

L11.lecture_goal: Analyze the factors that cause and the methods used to measure cybersickness.

objectives.text: You'll be able to identify and explain the content factors contributing to cybersickness.
You'll be able to classify and compare the various input types and measurement methods used to assess cybersickness.

L12.lecture_goal: Master the principles of cybersickness, from its causes and evaluation to its practical mitigation strategies.

objectives.text: You'll be able to evaluate the scientific framework and models used for predicting cybersickness by outlining evaluation frameworks and comparing different model types.
You'll be able to analyze and describe various strategies and techniques for mitigating cybersickness, including FOV adjustments, hardware solutions, and user-driven guidelines.
You'll be able to review the fundamental causes, measurement methods, and overall mitigation strategies of cybersickness.

L13.lecture_goal: Analyze the architecture and diverse input mechanisms that constitute a complete virtual reality hardware system.

objectives.text: You'll be able to explain the holistic components, data flow, and essential hardware categories of a complete VR system.
You'll be able to compare and contrast the five categories of VR hand input devices.
You'll be able to describe non-hand-based input mechanisms, including head tracking and eye tracking.

L14.lecture_goal: Analyze the various components and mechanisms that constitute a complete VR hardware system.

objectives.text: You'll be able to describe the methods and mechanisms of non-hand input devices.
You'll be able to identify and explain the function and selection criteria for VR processing elements.
You'll be able to compare and contrast the three main categories of visual displays used in VR systems.
You'll be able to differentiate between various categories of haptic and audio output devices.
You'll be able to compare types of motion platforms and summarize VR hardware components.

L15.lecture_goal: analyze the components, types, and principles of augmented reality hardware systems.

objectives.text: You'll be able to categorize and compare the various types of AR hardware, differentiating between AR and VR systems, smart glasses, and different AR system types.
You'll be able to define the characteristics of spatial AR, identify various hardware implementations, and contrast different AR display technologies like HUDs and contact lenses.
You'll be able to review and categorize the different types of AR hardware systems discussed throughout the lecture.

L16.lecture_goal: Understand the core concepts, classifications, and processes involved in tracking systems for AR and VR.

objectives.text: You'll be able to compare the specific requirements and functions of tracking in AR and VR systems.
You'll be able to classify tracking methods and compare the functional differences between outside-in and inside-out systems.
You'll be able to explain the four fundamental steps and identify the targets, methods, and stages of the tracking process.

L17.lecture_goal: Analyze the complete process of sensor tracking, from initial measurement to drift correction.

objectives.text: You'll be able to explain the fundamental concepts of tracking, including tracker types and the four stages of the process.
You'll be able to define the Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) and describe the process of calibrating its sensors using linear least squares.
You'll be able to explain how sensor orientation is calculated using registration and integration.
You'll be able to explain the mechanism of drift correction and summarize the key processes of calibration, registration, integration, and drift correction.

L18.lecture_goal: analyze the principles and applications of diverse tracking technologies used in various fields.

objectives.text: You'll be able to describe the structure and compare the operational principles of various electromechanical tracking devices, including electromagnetic, acoustic, and infrared systems.
You'll be able to differentiate between fiducial, natural feature, and model-based tracking techniques, and explain the mechanism of 3D structure tracking using commercial sensors.
You'll be able to differentiate between inertial and GPS tracking systems and their respective limitations, and describe the various types and mechanisms of motion and eye tracking systems.
You'll be able to summarize the core concepts of tracking and understand its transition into the study of VR software.

L19.lecture_goal: Analyze the core principles, components, and development challenges of VR software.

objectives.text: You'll be able to explain the fundamental role, data flow, and development approaches of VR software.
You'll be able to describe the function of the Virtual World Generator and the methods required for creating a virtual world.
You'll be able to explain the concepts of matched motion and locomotion support to ensure immersive and comfortable VR experiences.

L20.lecture_goal: Understand the complete lifecycle of VR software development, from foundational concepts to deployment strategies.

objectives.text: You'll be able to explain how the initial components of a virtual world generator and physics support function within a VR system.
You'll be able to identify the key components necessary to build a networked collaborative VR experience.
You'll be able to evaluate the trade-offs between building VR systems from scratch and utilizing ready-made engines, and describe the core structure of these engines.
You'll be able to differentiate between native and web deployment tools and their respective categories.
You'll be able to review the key concepts and development choices involved in VR software creation.

L21.lecture_goal: Analyze the structure, construction, and practical application of various AR software tools.

objectives.text: You'll be able to categorize AR software tools by required programming skill and explain how low-level AR frameworks are constructed using combined libraries.
You'll be able to describe the function and use of AR prototyping tools like FLAR Toolkit and FLAR Manager.

L22.lecture_goal: Explore the diverse landscape and operational methods of modern AR software development.

objectives.text: You'll be able to analyze the utility and limitations of various AR development tools, including non-flash prototyping methods and plugin-based systems.
You'll be able to describe the characteristics and functionality of standalone AR authoring tools.
You'll be able to summarize AR software categories and introduce the topic of human factors.

L23.lecture_goal: Analyze the principles of designing effective interactive systems by integrating human factors and user-centric approaches.

objectives.text: You'll be able to explain the relationship between XR, interactive systems, and the concept of disappearing technology, and analyze the negative impact of technical jargon on lay users.
You'll be able to describe the principles of a user-centric approach, define HCI, and compare different user types to demonstrate the necessity of incorporating human factors into system design.

L24.lecture_goal: Analyze the principles of usability and user-centered design to inform the development of effective interactive systems.

objectives.text: You'll be able to apply the novice, intermittent, and expert classification to inform design decisions and explain how software developers incorporate user needs into the design lifecycle.
You'll be able to explain the ISO definition of usability and its three crucial constraints, and define usability metrics and the principles of user-centered design.
You'll be able to describe the architecture and human factors of Extended Reality systems.
You'll be able to summarize the current topic and identify the next learning objective.

L25.lecture_goal: Analyze how human sensory and perceptual systems influence the design and outcomes of immersive XR technologies.

objectives.text: You'll be able to explain how perceptual psychology informs the design of effective XR systems by analyzing physiological mechanisms and presence principles.
You'll be able to identify and classify the various sensory receptors and their functions in the human body, including their corresponding stimuli and organs.

L26.lecture_goal: analyze the relationship between human physiological processes and effective design principles in immersive XR environments.

objectives.text: You'll be able to explain how perception operates, from the initial neural sensing and hierarchical pattern detection to the influence of long-term knowledge on stimulus interpretation.
You'll be able to describe the function of proprioception and explain the mechanism and effects of sensory mismatch within immersive XR systems.
You'll be able to summarize the lecture's focus on applying human physiology and perception principles to XR design.

L27.lecture_goal: Analyze the principles of light interaction and the physiological mechanisms that enable human visual perception.

objectives.text: You'll be able to explain how light propagates through the visual system in XR and describe the fundamental models of light, how light interacts with material surfaces, and the mechanism of color perception through its.

You'll be able to trace the path of light through the human eye, describe the structure and function of the eye's visual system, and compare the functions of rods and cones in determining vision quality.

You'll be able to explain the relationship between light wave properties and color perception, describe how photoreceptor density dictates central and peripheral vision capabilities, and explain the physiological cause.

L28.lecture_goal: Analyze the principles of visual perception and apply them to the design and functionality of modern extended reality (XR) systems.

objectives.text: You'll be able to identify the key components of the human eye and explain how its optical mechanisms achieve proper focus.
You'll be able to describe how binocular vision and VR optics enable depth perception and define the degrees of freedom in 3D space.
You'll be able to determine the physiological and technical considerations for designing XR displays, including resolution requirements and key design concepts.

L29.lecture_goal: Analyze how the physical properties of sound and the biological mechanisms of human hearing contribute to immersive experiences in extended reality.

objectives.text: You'll be able to identify the role of auditory senses and explain how auditory sense enhances immersion and presence in VR.
You'll be able to define sound and explain its physical properties and the physiological mechanism of human hearing.
You'll be able to understand why sound enhances presence and how the auditory system processes sound waves.

L30.lecture_goal: Analyze the principles of auditory perception and localization to design immersive and believable XR experiences.

objectives.text: You'll be able to explain the fundamental principles of auditory perception, including the levels of sound perception, key concepts, and psychophysical laws.
You'll be able to explain how sound localization is achieved and implemented in XR systems using binaural cues, MAA, and HRTF.
You'll be able to summarize the key concepts of sound perception and implementation in XR.

L31.lecture_goal: Explore how integrating non-visual senses enhances the realism and immersion of extended reality (XR) systems.

objectives.text: You'll be able to identify the remaining senses and explain their relevance to building immersive XR systems.
You'll be able to describe the mechanisms of somatosensory perception and compare various methods for providing haptic feedback in XR systems.
You'll be able to describe the mechanisms and challenges involved in simulating smell and taste within XR environments.
You'll be able to summarize the overall role of other senses in XR and preview interactive system development opportunities.

L32.lecture_goal: master the principles and stages of the Interactive System Development Life Cycle (ISDLC) for creating usable XR systems.

objectives.text: You'll be able to define user-centered design and explain its relationship to human factors in XR systems.
You'll be able to explain the necessity and function of the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC).
You'll be able to analyze the complexity of design choices and describe the highly iterative lifecycle and requirement gathering for usable interactive systems.
You'll be able to compare evaluation methods and understand the critical loops and stages of the ISDLC for building usable XR systems.

L33.lecture_goal: Analyze the challenges of cultural heritage preservation by applying the Majuli digital heritage case study.

objectives.text: You'll be able to identify the Majuli case study, describe its geographical and cultural features, and analyze the necessity of its preservation.
You'll be able to define digital heritage preservation, explain the role of immersive technologies, and outline the objectives of the Majuli case study.

L34.lecture_goal: Understand the scope, methodology, and technical challenges involved in developing the Majuli Island VR system.

objectives.text: You'll be able to identify the major concerns and issues for the Majuli Island VR system.
You'll be able to describe the methodology used to capture and structure the Majuli cultural heritage archive.
You'll be able to analyze the key technical and design challenges of the Majuli VR Tour project.

L35.lecture_goal: Master the principles and techniques for gathering and specifying usability requirements in system design.

objectives.text: You'll be able to compare and differentiate between system-centered and user-centered design approaches, and distinguish between end-user requirements, feasibility constraints, and functional/non-functional system type.
You'll be able to define usability and explain how contextual inquiry is used to gather and ensure a usable system design through practical application.

L36.lecture_goal: learn how to gather, analyze, and specify usability requirements using contextual inquiry and affinity diagram methods.

objectives.text: You'll be able to describe the methods and planning steps of contextual inquiry.
You'll be able to apply affinity diagram and sorting techniques to organize raw data and distinguish between usability requirements and implementation prescriptions.
You'll be able to specify and refine usability requirements for an application using structured observation data.

L37.lecture_goal: master the process of gathering, defining, and specifying usability requirements for system development.

objectives.text: You'll be able to apply contextual inquiry outcomes and usability findings to define, structure, and convert design guidelines into functional requirements within an SRS.
You'll be able to apply user research methods to define target audiences and explain how to mitigate specific usability challenges, such as cyber sickness, in VR/AR systems.
You'll be able to recap the entire process of usability requirement gathering and its application to a case study.

L38.lecture_goal: master the principles and practices required for effective interactive system design.

objectives.text: You'll be able to outline the stages of the interactive system development lifecycle and identify methods for interface and interaction design.
You'll be able to differentiate between generic and specific design guidelines and explain the concepts of internal and external consistency.
You'll be able to apply core usability principles, including universal design, feedback rules, error prevention, and cognitive load management.
You'll be able to identify and categorize interaction techniques used in extended reality.

L39.lecture_goal: understand the principles and techniques governing interaction, selection, and manipulation in immersive systems.

objectives.text: You'll be able to define the three types of interaction used in immersive experiences.
You'll be able to analyze and compare various techniques used for object selection in immersive environments.
You'll be able to compare and contrast various object manipulation techniques used in immersive environments.

L40.lecture_goal: Analyze the fundamental design principles governing navigation, wayfinding, and interaction in immersive virtual reality systems.

objectives.text: You'll be able to explain the principles of VR locomotion, comparing and classifying various movement techniques.
You'll be able to describe the concept of wayfinding and identify methods for providing effective support in complex virtual environments.
You'll be able to summarize the various interaction techniques used in immersive systems.

L41.lecture_goal: design a comprehensive virtual reality system by integrating theoretical knowledge, technical components, and user-centric design principles.

objectives.text: You'll be able to apply theoretical knowledge and user-centric principles to define the scope and initial design elements of a VR system.
You'll be able to describe the technical components and processes required to build and enhance a high-quality interactive VR system.
You'll be able to explain design techniques for optimizing the user experience, including minimizing cyber-sickness.

L42.lecture_goal: master the principles of iterative system design and prototyping throughout the development lifecycle.

objectives.text: You'll be able to identify the remaining step in the XR system development process and describe the iterative cycles and feedback loops necessary for interactive system design.
You'll be able to define prototypes and compare the differences between horizontal and vertical prototypes.
You'll be able to explain the characteristics and application of low-fidelity tools like storyboarding and interface sketches, and compare the three levels of prototyping fidelity.
You'll be able to explain the Wizard of Oz prototyping approach and its application.

L43.lecture_goal: Master the principles and procedures for both implementing and evaluating system prototypes.

objectives.text: You'll be able to differentiate between throwaway, incremental, and evolutionary prototyping methods.
You'll be able to describe and apply various prototype evaluation techniques, including quick expert evaluation, cognitive walkthrough, and heuristic evaluation.

L44.lecture_goal: Analyze the processes for developing, optimizing, and evaluating immersive VR systems.

objectives.text: You'll be able to compare and categorize techniques and questionnaires used to evaluate immersive XR experiences.
You'll be able to compare and contrast development strategies and implementation methods for VR systems.

L45.lecture_goal: Master the principles and methodology required to conduct conclusive empirical evaluations of interactive systems.

objectives.text: You'll be able to explain the role of empirical evaluation and outline the requirements and stages for conclusive usability evaluation.
You'll be able to frame testable research questions, distinguish between key variables, and outline the definition and initial stages of empirical research.

L46.lecture_goal: Apply the principles of experimental design and statistical analysis to conduct rigorous empirical studies.

objectives.text: You'll be able to explain the criteria for designing a reliable empirical study, including formulating testable questions, selecting representative participants, and comparing experimental designs.
You'll be able to determine the necessity of statistical testing and apply appropriate tests to draw valid conclusions from observed data.

L47.lecture_goal: Evaluate the process of system implementation and the empirical methods used to assess VR technology.

objectives.text: You'll be able to review the key concepts and stages of the system implementation and evaluation cycle.
You'll be able to describe the objectives, identify the components, and explain the procedure for conducting a controlled VR experiment.
You'll be able to interpret and analyze the experimental results concerning presence, prior experience, and cyber sickness.
You'll be able to summarize the findings and outline the procedure for empirical evaluation.

L48.lecture_goal: Compare traditional and modern system development methodologies to understand effective system implementation.

objectives.text: You'll be able to explain the stages of the system development life cycle, outline implementation processes, and identify the limitations of traditional sequential approaches.
You'll be able to compare the Agile development framework to traditional methods and summarize system implementation concepts, including optimization.

L49.lecture_goal: analyze the principles and techniques required to optimize VR experiences for both performance and user comfort.

objectives.text: You'll be able to explain the core challenges and trade-offs in VR optimization, including the relationship between cyber sickness and presence.
You'll be able to compare and analyze different VR control methods and techniques, such as matching visual speed to enhance realism.
You'll be able to summarize the overall VR optimization framework and articulate the importance of presence.

L50.lecture_goal: understand the process of developing and optimizing realistic walking models to minimize cyber sickness in virtual reality experiences.

objectives.text: You'll be able to outline the stages of developing a realistic walking behavior model and analyze the resulting walking speed patterns from collected data.
You'll be able to analyze the discrepancy between actual and perceived movement in virtual tours and explain the mechanisms for calculating perceived visual speed using visual gain.
You'll be able to summarize the realistic walking model and introduce approaches for minimizing cyber sickness in VR environments.

L51.lecture_goal: design and implement an efficient algorithm for minimizing travel time in semi-interactive VR tours using graph theory and the Traveling Salesman Problem.

objectives.text: You'll be able to explain the principles of optimizing VR experience by controlling exposure duration and analyze the methods and trade-offs involved in managing VR exposure.
You'll be able to define the characteristics of semi-interactive VR tours and compare different optimization approaches for designing efficient VR tours.

You'll be able to model the optimal travel path problem by defining the graph structure and objective, deriving the travel time formula, and adapting the Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) for non-complete graphs.
You'll be able to describe and summarize the two-stage algorithm used to solve the TSP on a non-complete graph to minimize travel time.

L52.lecture_goal: understand the theoretical framework and practical algorithms used to optimize VR pathfinding for enhanced user experience.

objectives.text: You'll be able to compare path optimization methods by introducing the time threshold constraint, formulate the importance of nodes and paths, and calculate total waiting time for a path.
You'll be able to define the VR path optimization problem using the Vehicle Routing Problem with Profit (VRPP) and outline the multi-stage algorithm for optimizing VR pathfinding with wait times.
You'll be able to summarize the advanced pathfinding methods for optimizing VR experience and mitigating cyber sickness.

L53.lecture_goal: Apply optimization techniques and graph theory to design efficient VR experiences.

objectives.text: You'll be able to contrast different optimization approaches and define the specific goals for creating an efficient VR tour path.
You'll be able to describe the procedure for converting a real-world site into a graph and apply optimization algorithms (TSP/VRPP) to find efficient paths.
You'll be able to summarize the core concepts of VR experience and resource optimization.

L54.lecture_goal: understand the principles and technical challenges of optimizing virtual reality systems through efficient graphics rendering.

objectives.text: You'll be able to define the goals of VR optimization and identify the resources and hardware constraints involved.
You'll be able to explain the fundamentals of computer graphics, including rendering challenges and the architecture of a graphics system.
You'll be able to compare rendering methods and describe how raster scan displays refresh and manage color information.
You'll be able to review color perception and introduce the structure of the 3D graphics pipeline.

L55.lecture_goal: Understand how the 3D graphics pipeline is structured and optimized to meet the demanding resource requirements of virtual reality.

objectives.text: You'll be able to explain the function of the 3D graphics pipeline and describe its five stages and coordinate transformations.
You'll be able to analyze the trade-off between object realism and rendering efficiency in VR systems.
You'll be able to describe 3D object representation techniques and understand the structure and flexibility of the graphics pipeline stages.

L56.lecture_goal: understand how the 3D graphics pipeline processes geometry and simulates realistic color perception through lighting models.

objectives.text: You'll be able to review the graphics pipeline and apply basic and composite transformations to position objects in a world coordinate system.
You'll be able to explain lighting models and compute the ambient, diffuse, and specular light components using vector math.
You'll be able to model complex lighting scenarios, including intensity attenuation and summation from multiple light sources, and map continuous intensity values to finite device values.

L57.lecture_goal: master the principles of the 3D viewing pipeline to optimize VR resource rendering.

objectives.text: You'll be able to review the 3D graphics pipeline and understand how 3D scenes are projected onto 2D screens.
You'll be able to explain the stages of the 3D viewing pipeline, define projection types, and apply canonical view volumes.
You'll be able to describe the complete sequence of transformations from world space to the viewport and explain how clipping reduces computational complexity.

L58.lecture_goal: understand the principles and architectural components required to optimize 3D graphics rendering for virtual reality.

objectives.text: You'll be able to describe the fundamental stages of the 3D graphics pipeline, including scan conversion and efficient line rendering.
You'll be able to analyze the computational challenges inherent in rendering realistic and dynamic VR environments.
You'll be able to explain how graphics APIs, layered system architectures, and parallel GPU processing enable modern 3D rendering.

L59.lecture_goal: understand how resource optimization techniques are applied to deploy large-scale VR applications.

objectives.text: You'll be able to apply theoretical knowledge to define the scope of the Majuli virtual tour project.
You'll be able to explain the computational challenges of large-scale VR content and how cloud computing and deployment constraints necessitate various optimization strategies.
You'll be able to summarize the necessity of resource optimization and the role of computer graphics in VR deployment.

L60.lecture_goal: Implement theoretical XR knowledge using the Unity platform.

objectives.text: You'll be able to understand why theoretical XR knowledge must be linked to practical system implementation.
You'll be able to identify the coding stage and describe the Unity platform, its components, and its role in simplifying graphics pipeline implementation.
You'll be able to differentiate between core XR system types and Unity views, and define fundamental concepts such as Game Objects and Prefabs.

L61.lecture_goal: understand how Unity integrates various systems—from rendering and physics to animation and audio—to build complex interactive experiences.

objectives.text: You'll be able to explain how Unity implements the graphics pipeline, including object representation, scene setup, and the utilization of native APIs.
You'll be able to explain how rigid bodies, colliders, joints, and articulation create realistic physics within the environment.
You'll be able to describe Unity's components and workflows for implementing animation and audio systems.

L62.lecture_goal: Master the process of linking theoretical programming concepts to practical development methods within the Unity environment.

objectives.text: You'll be able to explain how to set up the Unity environment and implement fundamental C# scripting to control object behavior, including using event functions, conditionals, loops, and advanced timing methods.
You'll be able to apply scripting and integration knowledge to deploy systems and build complex applications, such as marker-based AR, by integrating external SDKs.

L63.lecture_goal: Understand the course structure and the scope of XR disciplines.

objectives.text: You'll be able to explain the content and structure of the Foundation for XR Systems course.
You'll be able to understand the foundational objective and scope of XR disciplines.
